Growing roses in clay soil

Clay soil holds water and nutrients well, which roses like, but it drains slowly and packs hard in summer. Our members dig in two to three inches of compost every autumn and plant on a slight mound so the crown never sits in standing water.

Mulch with shredded bark after the first frost, water deeply once a week rather than a little every day, and prune in early spring when the forsythia blooms. Old garden roses and rugosas are the most forgiving choices for beginners.

Next meeting: the first Saturday of the month at the community hall. Visitors are always welcome.
